fees_page.title: Fees & Rules
fees_page.subtitle: Understanding platform fees, processing costs, and payout schedules.
fees_page.who_pays_intro: It depends on where your event is, and it is not a setting you choose. Each market follows what buyers there expect.
fees_page.who_pays_us_a: the fee is added on top at checkout, so you receive the
fees_page.who_pays_us_b: . Price a ticket at $20 and you receive $20; your buyer sees the total, with the fee shown as a separate line, before they pay.
fees_page.who_pays_ht_a: the buyer pays exactly the price you advertised and the fee comes out of your proceeds. Price a ticket at 1,000 HTG and the buyer pays 1,000 HTG, of which you receive
fees_page.who_pays_ht_b: . An advertised price carries trust in a cash-oriented market, so it means what it says.
fees_page.who_pays_free_note: Free events are never charged a fee under either model.
fees_page.platform_fee_b: on paid ticket sales in the United States, Canada and France, and
fees_page.platform_fee_c: in Haiti. This helps us maintain and improve the platform, provide customer support, and continue developing new features.
fees_page.flat_strong: the same percentage on every ticket
fees_page.flat_b: , with no cap, however much the ticket costs: a $200 ticket carries {{usExample}} and a 20,000 HTG ticket carries {{htExample}}.
fees_page.who_chooses_a: You choose who pays it. By default, buyers in the United States, Canada and France pay it on top of your price, and in Haiti it comes out of your payout, but every event has a
fees_page.pass_fee_switch: Pass the service fee to buyers
fees_page.who_chooses_b: switch, so the choice is yours per event.
fees_page.processing_intro: Payment processing fees vary by payment method:
fees_page.processing_note: Tikèm pays these out of its own fee, in every country and whoever bears the fee. They are never added to your buyer's total or deducted from your payout.
fees_page.schedule_b: . This holding period allows time for any refund requests or payment disputes to be resolved.
fees_page.schedule_c: Once the holding period is complete, you can request a payout from your organizer dashboard. Payouts are typically processed within
fees_page.note_body: For free events, there are no fees charged. Platform and processing fees only apply to paid ticket sales.

page.title: Delete your Tikèm account
page.lede: You can delete your account yourself at any time, in the app or on the web. Deletion takes effect immediately.
page.app_steps: Open the app, go to Profile, scroll to the bottom and tap Delete account. Type DELETE to confirm.
page.web_steps: Sign in at tikem.co, open your Profile, and under Account choose Delete account. Type DELETE to confirm.
page.reauth_note: If you signed in more than a few minutes ago, we'll ask you to confirm it's you first.
page.deleted_body: Your sign-in and account, profile and photo, saved events and favorites, follows, reviews, notifications and push tokens, event-staff access, identity-verification uploads, and saved payout details (bank account and MonCash number).
page.kept_body: Tickets stay attached to their event so its attendance and sales records remain accurate. Orders, payments, refunds and payouts are kept as financial records for as long as accounting and tax law requires. Your name, email and phone are removed from all of them, and payout destinations are reduced to their last four digits.
page.organizers_body: If you have upcoming events with sold tickets, money waiting to be withdrawn, a withdrawal in progress, or promoter earnings, we'll list what to resolve first: cancel and refund those events, and withdraw your balance. We never delete an account while buyers' tickets or money depend on it.
page.support_body: Email {{email}} from the address on your account and we'll delete it for you.
